report.scope: US market, lab-grown and natural diamonds, 1–10 carats total weight, mostly 14K gold. Prices seen online on Nov 13, 2026, two weeks before Black Friday.

primer.what_it_is: A flexible bracelet of matching diamonds set in a continuous line, sold by total carat weight (ct tw): the combined weight of every stone.

must_haves.feature: Box clasp with a safety catch
must_haves.why: A figure-8 or fold-over safety stops the bracelet falling off if the clasp pops.
Holds stones securely for decades; silver and 10K wear faster.
Stones of the same color and size look like one line of light.
Color and clarity (e.g. F-G / VS2-SI1) tell you what you're paying for.

premium_features.why: Buys rarity and tradition, not a look; costs 1.8–2.9x lab at 5 ct.
More secure than two or three prongs for daily wear.
Heavier and naturally white; costs more than 14K white gold.

avoid.why: Soft prongs bend, so stones loosen.
Many tiny dull stones fake a bigger look.
The original price is set so the sale looks big.

verdict.headline: Buy lab-grown in 14K online; 5 ct costs barely more than 2–3 ct, and Black Friday is two weeks away.
verdict.confidence: Moderate: about 18 listings priced across seven sellers; Costco US and price history were not seen.
verdict.reasoning: Lab-grown 14K bracelets with F-G / VS2-SI1 stones now cost $675–$830 per carat at 5 ct, against $1,150–$1,940 for natural. Per-carat price falls as total weight rises, so the 5 ct lab bracelet is the sweet spot. Mall natural bracelets cost up to $3,220 per carat for the same look.
verdict.price_watch_summary: Blue Nile's 5 ct lab bracelet is $3,374 (30% off $4,820); aim for $3,000 or less during Black Friday, Nov 27–30.

recommendation.product: Blue Nile 7" Two-Prong Lab-Grown Tennis Bracelet, 14K white gold, 5 ct tw (F-G / VS2-SI1)
recommendation.why: Graded 14K lab stones at the lowest per-carat price seen; a holiday promo near 38% off reaches $3,000.

normalization.unit: Price per carat of total diamond weight, compared within the same diamond type, grade and metal
normalization.unit_rationale: Shoppers compare sticker prices, but a $2,000 bracelet can hold 1 ct or 10 ct. Price per carat shows that bigger lab bracelets are cheaper per carat, and that mall natural pieces cost 2–4x online lab.
normalization.quality_adjustment: Compare like with like: lab vs. natural, 14K vs. 10K or silver, and the stated grade. Natural at the same grade costs about 1.8–2.9x lab; silver and 10K should cost clearly less than 14K.
normalization.formula: Value = price ÷ total carats, then compared only against the same diamond type, metal and grade

normalization.size_economics: Per-carat prices fall as total weight rises: Brilliant Earth lab is $1,895 per carat at 1 ct, $983 at 3 ct and $830 at 5 ct. Moving from 2 ct to 5 ct lab adds only a few hundred dollars on sale.

diminishing_returns.below_knee: Below ~$500 per carat you drop to sterling silver, 10K gold or ungraded stones: weaker prongs or unknown sparkle.
diminishing_returns.above_knee: Above ~$900 per carat you mostly pay for natural origin, small-size labor or a mall brand, not a better-looking bracelet.

spec_criteria.what_good_looks_like: 14K gold or platinum; box clasp plus figure-8 or fold-over safety
spec_criteria.how_to_check: Metal line in the title; clasp photos or the specs tab
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: Prongs and clasp are what fail; 14K holds stones for decades

spec_criteria.what_good_looks_like: Color G-H or better, clarity SI1 or better (I1 acceptable only if inspected)
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: Low color looks yellow; low clarity looks dull in small stones

spec_criteria.what_good_looks_like: Whichever you chose, priced against its own kind
spec_criteria.how_to_check: "Lab-grown" in the title; natural is usually just "diamond"
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: Natural costs 1.8–2.9x more for the same look

spec_criteria.what_good_looks_like: Four prongs for daily wear; two or three is fine for occasional wear
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: More prongs mean less chance of losing a stone

spec_criteria.what_good_looks_like: Even size and color along the line
spec_criteria.how_to_check: 360° video or in person; uneven stones show at arm's length
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: A tennis bracelet reads as one line of light

spec_criteria.what_good_looks_like: IGI or GIA report covering the bracelet
spec_criteria.why_it_matters: Without one, the grade is the seller's word
Too tight stresses the clasp; too loose catches

marketing_noise.reality: Total weight of all stones; says nothing about grade or metal.
Mall reference prices few people pay; compare price per carat instead.
Resale is a fraction of retail for natural and near zero for lab.

value_traps.instead: Pay about $1,000 more for 10K or 14K gold if you'll wear it daily.

value_traps.why_it_isnt: Many tiny I2-I3 stones grouped to look bigger; dull up close.
value_traps.instead: Buy a lab line bracelet with a stated grade.

value_traps.why_it_isnt: Per carat it costs 2x more ($1,895 vs. $983), and natural is only $600 more at 1 ct.
value_traps.instead: Go natural at 1 ct, or step up to 5 ct lab for the best per-carat price.

value_traps.why_it_looks_good: Natural diamonds feel like they hold value
value_traps.why_it_isnt: Retail markups mean resale is a fraction of the price.
value_traps.instead: Buy natural only if origin matters to you emotionally.

tiers.verdict: Fine starter; upgrade metal for daily wear
The value zone, especially at 5 ct
Same look online for about half

consensus.expert_view: Buying guides agree lab-grown is the value choice for tennis bracelets, where small stones make lab and natural indistinguishable; the clasp and prongs matter most for wear.
consensus.community_view: Owners recommend online sellers over malls, insist on a box clasp with a safety catch, and treat lab bracelets as everyday jewelry rather than an asset.
consensus.where_they_disagree: Some still favor natural for heirlooms and resale, though resale values don't support the price gap.

deal_intelligence.volatility: High: online jewelers run 30–40% promotions often, and lab-grown prices keep falling year over year.
deal_intelligence.best_time_to_buy: Black Friday to Cyber Monday, Nov 27–30, 2026.
deal_intelligence.patience_payoff: Waiting two weeks could save about $375 on the Blue Nile 5 ct lab bracelet ($3,374 to $3,000).
deal_intelligence.discount_honesty: Online list prices are anchors (Blue Nile $4,820 list, sold at $3,374); mall "50% off" prices start even higher. Judge every deal by price per carat.
